packet.claim: The recovery kernel's cell grammar and rewrite execution are inconsistent for inputs with a fenced object followed by prose or another object.
packet.execution_evidence: The provided test campaign results show INVALID_INSTANTIATION for proposals 6e926231a6feb78e, 23cf9366607b4a9d, 5f53e9aa9d4584e4, d0a99f69c34e90f2, b0c18ec3f659b3e7, 4661b792a4b41075, ef032f8da4e09e38, and others.
packet.expected: Rewrites that add content after a fence should be valid instantiations and should move the recovered object when the added content is a later top-level object, or remain unchanged when the added content is prose.
packet.observed: Several rewrites are reported as INVALID_INSTANTIATION with details like 'the rewritten text is no cell of the grammar' or 'the input is not the cell it names', even when the rewritten text contains a valid later top-level object.
packet.scope: Inputs where a fenced JSON object is followed by prose or additional top-level objects, and a rewrite adds content after the fence.
packet.source_basis: recover_json_object: 'Every top-level balanced object in the text is a candidate... The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text.'
packet.uncertainty: The exact cell grammar rules are not fully specified in the provided documentation, so some INVALID_INSTANTIATION results may be intended if the grammar only permits certain sequences of fenced and unfenced parts.
